user-1.text: Show me the formatting you can use in replies.

text-2.markdown:
Here is how the new message formatting looks.

> [!NOTE]
> The recorder keeps plugin names but renames them to plugin-a…j.

> [!TIP]
> Pass `--skip-terminal-check` when you run the app inside tmux.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Ask before every commit and push.

> [!WARNING]
> The file transport writes temporary files; they are removed after sending.

> [!CAUTION]
> `git push --force` rewrites the shared history.

The palette now uses `#7fa6f5` for the accent, `#f7a` for highlights, `rgb(232, 197, 71)` for warnings and `hsl(230 22% 13%)` for panels. Errors used plain `red` before, and issue #123 tracks the rest.

The pairwise pass costs $O(n^2)$ because every pair computes $\alpha \cdot d_{ij}$. The mean squared error:

$$E = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$$

With $\beta \leq 0.5$ the result improves by up to $\sqrt{2}$. The upgrade costs $5 and $10 per seat.

Undo with Ctrl+Z, redo with `Ctrl+Shift+Z`, and close a dialog with <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

I changed the image transport to temporary files.

<details><summary>Measurements</summary>

Before: 5.4 MB/s while scrolling, frames up to 149 ms.
After: 0.04 MB/s, 3.4 ms median frame.
OpenTUI numbers images by their position in the frame,
so an image above scrolling out re-sends every image below it.

</details>

This change keeps image blocks out of the tool result text:

```diff
@@ -50,7 +50,9 @@ function toolResultText(
 function toolResultText(content: string | ToolResultBlock[] | undefined): string {
   if (content === undefined) return ""
   if (typeof content === "string") return content
-  return content.map((block) => (block.type === "text" ? (block.text ?? "") : `[${block.type}]`)).join("\n")
+  return content
+    .flatMap((block) => (block.type === "text" ? [block.text ?? ""] : []))
+    .join("\n")
 }
```

Here is src/ui/diff.ts:

```ts
import type { Hunk } from "../session/types.ts"

export type DiffRow = { kind: "add" | "del" | "ctx"; number: number; text: string } | { kind: "gap" }

// Keeps `context` unchanged lines around each change; dropped lines become a single gap row.
export function diffRows(hunks: readonly Hunk[], context = 1): DiffRow[] {
  const rows: DiffRow[] = []
  for (const hunk of hunks) {
    let oldLine = hunk.oldStart
    let newLine = hunk.newStart
    const lines: Extract<DiffRow, { number: number }>[] = []
    for (const line of hunk.lines) {
      const text = line.slice(1)
      if (line.startsWith("+")) lines.push({ kind: "add", number: newLine++, text })
      else if (line.startsWith("-")) lines.push({ kind: "del", number: oldLine++, text })
      else if (line.startsWith(" ")) {
        lines.push({ kind: "ctx", number: newLine, text })
        oldLine++
        newLine++
      }
    }
    const keep = lines.map(
      (row, index) =>
        row.kind !== "ctx" ||
        lines.slice(Math.max(0, index - context), index + context + 1).some((near) => near.kind !== "ctx"),
    )
    lines.forEach((row, index) => {
      if (!keep[index]) return
      if ((index === 0 || !keep[index - 1]) && rows.length > 0) rows.push({ kind: "gap" })
      rows.push(row)
    })
  }
  return rows
}

export function addedRows(content: string): DiffRow[] {
  return content
    .replace(/\n$/, "")
    .split("\n")
    .map((text, index) => ({ kind: "add", number: index + 1, text }))
}
```

The key part is diffRows: it turns hunks into rows.
